cues.en: but boy did they pack a lot of features into this white sheet metal box.

cues.en: For a start, the user interface is radically different from microwaves both contemporary to its time and now.

cues.en: menu system for its various functions.

cues.en: And did the designers have fun with that display?

cues.zh: 当然啦！

cues.en: Just look what happens when you plug it in.

cues.en: Delightful.

cues.en: When in use, the time-remaining display takes the form of a giant animated hourglass,

cues.zh: 为什么不呢？
cues.en: because why not?

cues.zh: 谁能不爱呢？
cues.en: What’s not to love?

cues.en: Ah, the nineties.

cues.zh: 你真是青绿、粉色和紫色的巅峰。
cues.en: You truly were the teal, pink, and purple best.

cues.zh: 总之，除了九十年代中期微波炉里那块带成熟菜单系统的点阵显示屏十足新奇之外，
cues.en: Anyway, aside from the sheer novelty of a dot-matrix display with a mature menu system

cues.en: in a microwave from the mid-nineties, there’s a lot of smarts included, too.

cues.zh: 不过说句公道话，很多微波炉都有*一些*自动烹饪或加热的能力。
cues.en: Now, to be fair, lots of microwaves have *some* ability to cook or reheat things automatically.

cues.zh: 门上通常贴着一张表，列出每个类别的不同设置，

cues.zh: 而且你可能还有几个专门针对某些食物的快捷键。
cues.en: and you may very well have a few dedicated buttons for certain things.

cues.zh: 但这把它提升到了一个新层次。
cues.en: But this takes it to the next level.

cues.en: There are dozens of options for things you can cook with this, from potatoes

cues.en: (white or sweet),

cues.en: to bacon, to squash (winter or summer),

cues.en: eggs all these ways (with instructions, as well),

cues.en: and even artichokes!

cues.en: And they all work excellently.

cues.zh: 你看，给微波炉编程实现自动化其实并不特别难
cues.en: See, it’s not particularly difficult to program automation into a microwave oven

cues.zh: 只需要一个湿度传感器做反馈。
cues.en: with just a single humidity sensor for feedback.

cues.zh: 拿爆米花举例吧。
cues.en: Let’s use popcorn as an example.

cues.zh: 毕竟微波爆米花太重要了，几乎总是有专属按钮，连这里也不例外。
cues.en: After all, microwave popcorn is so important it almost always gets its own button, even here.

cues.zh: 当你按下爆米花按钮时，让许多袋爆米花叫苦不迭的是，
cues.en: When you use the popcorn button, much to the chagrin of many bags of popcorn,

cues.zh: 微波炉一开始只是让风扇运转一段固定时间。
cues.en: the microwave starts out by simply running its fans for a set period of time.

cues.zh: 磁控管不通电，所以并没有在加热，它利用这段时间清除
cues.en: The magnetron isn’t powered thus cooking isn’t occurring, and it uses this period to clear out any moisture

cues.zh: 传感器附近的湿气，并建立一个基线读数。
cues.en: near the sensor and establish a baseline reading.

cues.zh: 这一步之后，它会启动磁控管并观察传感器。
cues.en: After this step, it switches on the magnetron and watches the sensor.

cues.zh: 一袋微波爆米花通常会在开始爆裂时保持密封一段时间，
cues.en: A bag of microwave popcorn typically stays sealed for a while as it starts to pop,

cues.zh: 所以传感器看不到变化，
cues.en: so the sensor won’t see a change,

cues.zh: 但压力最终会累积，袋子的密封就会爆开。[轻微爆裂声]
cues.en: but eventually the pressure builds and the bag’s seal bursts. [low poof sound]

cues.zh: 一团蒸汽从袋中冒出，传感器会立刻检测到。
cues.en: A cloud of steam exits the bag which the sensor will pick up right away.

cues.zh: 接下来就是有趣的部分了。
cues.en: Now here comes the fun part.

cues.zh: 微波炉可以用查找表，根据袋子爆开所用的时间来估算剩余的烹饪时间。
cues.en: The microwave can use a lookup table to estimate the remaining cooking time based upon how long it took for the bag to burst.

cues.zh: 小袋爆米花会更快开始爆裂，因此蒸汽传感器会更早读到蒸汽，
cues.en: A smaller bag of popcorn will start popping faster and thus the steam sensor will read steam sooner,

cues.zh: 而大袋爆米花需要更长时间才能爆开，所以要更久才能看到蒸汽。
cues.en: and a larger bag of popcorn will take more time to pop so it takes longer to see the steam.

cues.zh: 你只需要磁控管开启到检测到蒸汽之间的时间
cues.en: All you need is the time between magnetron switch-on and steam detection

cues.zh: 就能准确判断还需要多久才能爆完。
cues.en: to have a solid idea of how much longer it needs to finish popping.

cues.zh: 而这效果非常好，你几乎可以把任何尺寸的任何一袋爆米花扔进这台微波炉
cues.en: And this works so well that you can throw nearly any bag of popcorn of any size in this microwave

cues.zh: 它总能完全爆开，而且从不烧焦。
cues.en: and it will always completely pop and never burn.

cues.zh: 无需猜测。
cues.en: No guesswork needed.

cues.zh: 许多微波炉都有爆米花按钮，说得客气点，那玩意儿就是垃圾。
cues.en: Many microwave ovens have popcorn buttons which are, to put it nicely, bullshirt.

cues.zh: 如果你的微波炉要你告诉它爆米花袋有多大，
cues.en: If your microwave wants you to tell it how big the bag of popcorn is,

cues.zh: 那它很可能根本没用传感器，而是偷懒采用了
cues.en: well then it’s probably not using a sensor for anything and instead got the lazy treatment

cues.zh: 根据输入重量预设时间的做法。
cues.en: of pre-programmed times based on the inputted weight.

cues.zh: 这正是为什么有人告诉你别用爆米花按钮，
cues.en: This is precisely why you are told not to use the popcorn button,

cues.zh: 不过确实还有微波炉为爆米花配备了正经的传感器烹饪功能。
cues.en: however microwaves do still exist with proper sensor-cooking for popcorn.

cues.zh: 三星的型号似乎做得相当不错，至少在我有限的两次样本里是这样。
cues.en: Samsung models seem to do it fairly well, at least in my limited sample size of two.

cues.zh: 但不管怎样，你可以把这套逻辑套用到几乎任何你能想到的食物上。
cues.en: But anyway, you can apply this logic to virtually any food item you can imagine.

cues.zh: 只需要一些实验、分类，再建立查找表。
cues.en: All it takes is some experimentation, categorization, and creation of lookup tables.

cues.zh: 对你想要做成一键选项的每种食物都这样做，你就能实现真正的自动烹饪。
cues.en: Do this for each kind of food you want to make a one-touch option and you’ll have true automatic cooking.

cues.zh: 再说一次，并不是说现在市面上在售的微波炉都做不了某些形式的自动烹饪，
cues.en: And again, it’s not like no microwaves on sale today can do some forms of auto-cooking,

cues.zh: 但我不知道有哪个主流型号能像这台一样多功能，
cues.en: but I don’t know of any mainstream models that are as versatile as this one,

cues.zh: 更别说还这么好用了。
cues.en: let alone as easy to use.

cues.zh: 每个自动设置都是一键操作，如果有任何特殊说明
cues.en: Each auto-setting is one touch, and if there are any special instructions

cues.zh: 它们就在那儿等着你。
cues.en: they’re right there waiting for you.

cues.zh: 别以为这只是包装过的预编程定时器，并不是。
cues.en: And lest you think this is just dressed-up pre-programmed timers, it’s not.

cues.en: And my grandmother used its automatic functions extensively, and they never failed.

cues.zh: 每次都一样。
cues.en: Every time.

cues.en: Oh, and it’s not just cooking until it sees steam like for popcorn.

cues.zh: 根据所烹饪的食物，它可以让磁控管以不同功率循环工作，
cues.en: Depending on the item it cooks, it can cycle the magnetron at different power levels

cues.en: to achieve the best results it can.

cues.en: they’re few and far between.

cues.en: Truly I don’t know why this isn’t just, like, standard fare in microwaves these days.

cues.zh: 这技术肯定不算新。
cues.en: This tech surely ain’t new.

cues.zh: 一点也不新。
cues.en: Not at all.

cues.zh: 当然，还有一些不错的物联网点子流传着，
cues.en: Of course, there are some nifty Internet of Things ideas floating around

cues.en: And, yeah, that’s a neat idea, sure, but there’s a lot you can do with just a basic sensor and a bit of read-only memory.

cues.en: This microwave proves it without a doubt.

cues.en: It’s even got ratatouille in here, how fancy!

cues.zh: 不过说真的，这挺妙的。
cues.en: Seriously, though, this is pretty neat.

cues.zh: 它们是按步骤设计的，每一步都会让微波炉运行
cues.en: They’re designed to be followed step-by-step, and at each step it will run the microwave

cues.zh: 要么是预设的一段时间，要么甚至用上传感器。
cues.en: for either a predetermined period of time or even use the sensor.

cues.zh: 这确实很花哨，但确实有一种“智能家电”的风范，说实话，
cues.en: Now this is absolutely gimmicky, but there is a definite flair of “smart appliance” that, honestly,

cues.zh: 似乎比现在市面上许多所谓的智能家电要聪明得多。
cues.en: seems a lot smarter than many of the so-called smart appliances you can buy today.

cues.zh: 我的意思是，就像我说的，看看家装店里卖的微波炉。
cues.en: I mean, like I said, look at microwaves for sale in a home improvement store.

cues.zh: 没有一台像这台这么先进。
cues.en: None of them are as advanced as this one.

cues.zh: 在我看来，从这台微波炉制造出来到今天，微波炉领域唯一真正的创新
cues.en: As far as I’m concerned, the only true innovation in microwaves between when this was made and today

cues.zh: 就是松下用逆变器以较低功率驱动磁控管，
cues.en: is Panasonic’s use of an inverter to drive the magnetron at lower power levels,

cues.zh: 而不是像大多数微波炉（包括这台）那样，只是以不同的占空比循环开关。
cues.en: rather than just cycle it on and off at varying duty cycles like most including this one do.

cues.zh: 但综合来看，这算是个相当小众的优势。
cues.en: But that’s a pretty niche benefit all things considered.

cues.zh: 现在，如果你想知道我为什么会有我奶奶的旧微波炉，那让我告诉你。
cues.en: Now, if you’re wondering why I have my grandma’s old microwave, well let me tell ya.

cues.zh: 真的，全靠它那点小调子。
cues.en: Really, it’s all down to that little ditty it does.

cues.zh: 我至今还记得去爷爷奶奶家过圣诞或感恩节
cues.en: I have fond memories of visiting Grandma and Grandpa for Christmas or Thanksgiving

cues.zh: 听这台微波炉用最悦耳有趣的方式宣告加热完成。
cues.en: and hearing this microwave announce its doneness in the most pleasant and fun way.

cues.zh: 后来他们搬了新家，用的是炉灶上方那种微波炉，
cues.en: When they moved to a new home with an over-the-stove microwave situation,

cues.zh: 我就抢先认领了。
cues.en: well I called dibs.

cues.zh: 说实话我平时不用这台，因为我也处在炉灶上方微波炉的处境，幸好我现有的那台还凑合。
cues.en: And truthfully I don’t use this because I’m in the same microwave-over-the-stove situation, and luckily what I have is decent enough.

cues.zh: 所以目前它只是个备用，但我依然惊叹这东西有多先进。
cues.en: So for now it’s a spare, but I still absolutely marvel at how advanced this thing is.

cues.zh: 不过我有几点小抱怨。
cues.en: I do have a few quibbles, though.

cues.zh: 比如数字键盘。
cues.en: Like, for instance, the number pad.

cues.zh: 不。别——
cues.en: No. Do not-

cues.zh: 别这么搞——
cues.en: Do not do thi -

cues.zh: 设计师们听到了吗？
cues.en: You hear me designers?

cues.zh: 别这么搞。
cues.en: Do not do this.

cues.zh: 要么按计算器布局，要么按电话布局，别想着打破这个惯例，
cues.en: Everything should either be calculator or phone arrangement, don’t try and break that mold,

cues.zh: 行吗？
cues.en: OK?

cues.zh: 说真的，输入时间真烦人。
cues.en: Seriously, entering a time is annoying.

cues.zh: 而且显示屏本身也挺暗的，不过我觉得部分原因可能是老化。
cues.en: Also, the display itself is rather dim, though I suppose some of that could be down to age.

cues.zh: 毕竟它插着电亮了将近20年。
cues.en: This was plugged in and lit up for nearly 20 years straight, after all.

cues.zh: 另外，我觉得让时钟在屏幕上更显眼会更好，
cues.en: Also, I think it would have been better to make the clock more dominating on the screen,

cues.zh: 而不是就把它塞在角落里。
cues.en: rather than just shove it in the corner.

cues.zh: 尤其是因为它在闲置时会让屏幕变暗。
cues.en: Especially because it dims the screen when idle.

cues.zh: 不过也不是每个人都需要再多一个要设置的时钟。
cues.en: Not that everybody needs another clock to set, though.

cues.zh: 而且它确实会显示日期，这点还挺不错的。
cues.en: Plus it does show you the date, that's kinda nice.

cues.zh: 当然，整体来说这个设计也没那么经久耐看。
cues.en: And also, to be sure, the design hasn’t aged all that well in general.

cues.zh: 流线型造型早已过时了
cues.en: Swoopy shapes have gone the way of the dodo

cues.zh: ——一种特别流线的鸟——
cues.en: - a particularly swoopy bird -

cues.zh: 而且白色家电整体上现在也不太流行了。
cues.en: and white appliances as a whole are kinda not in at the moment.

cues.zh: 当然，还有它有点发黄了。这也是我怀疑白色家电差不多过时的主要原因之一。
cues.en: Plus, of course, it’s yellowing a bit. One of the main reasons I suspect white appliances are kinda over.

cues.zh: 不锈钢和黑色也许显得冷冰冰，但它会一直保持漂亮又冷峻。
cues.en: Stainless steel and black may be cold but it’ll be nice and cold forever.

cues.zh: 不过，我始终困惑于这种设计为何一直如此鲜为人知。
cues.en: But anyway, I remain perplexed at why this design has remained so obscure.

cues.zh: 我猜很多人根本不使用微波炉的自动功能，
cues.en: I imagine that many people just don’t use their microwave’s auto functions,

cues.zh: 毕竟许多冷冻食品都有特别的制备说明，经过足够多的试错，你自己就能摸索出门道。
cues.en: as after all many frozen meals will have special preparation instructions and after enough trial and error you’ll figure stuff out for yourself.

cues.zh: 但我确实想知道，如果自动功能不那么晦涩难懂，人们会不会更愿意使用它们。
cues.en: But I do wonder if people would be more inclined to use the automatic functions if they weren’t so cryptic.

cues.zh: 我是说，查阅炉门内侧的图表并不是最以用户为中心的设计。
cues.en: I mean, consulting a chart inside the door isn’t the most user-focused design.

cues.zh: 而且，这都2020年了。
cues.en: And like, it’s 2020.

cues.zh: 全彩LCD面板成本也就2美元左右。
cues.en: Full color LCD panels cost like $2.

cues.zh: 大多数微波炉还停留在七段数码管显示上，我实在想不通。
cues.en: Why most microwaves are stuck to seven-segment displays is beyond me.

cues.zh: 嘿，这台微波炉证明了它不需要连接互联网，对吧？
cues.en: And hey, this microwave proves that it doesn’t need to be connected to the Internet, OK?

cues.zh: 联网并不等于智能家电。
cues.en: Being online does not a smart appliance make.

cues.zh: 我敢说这比那些贵得离谱的微波炉都更聪明，
cues.en: I’d call this smarter than all but the most absurdly priced microwaves,

cues.zh: 而且它说不定还比这个“扫描即烹饪”技术更好用。
cues.en: and heck it still might work better than this Scan-To-Cook technology.

cues.zh: 如果在制造时就融入巧思，
cues.en: If you put the ingenuity in at the time of manufacture,

cues.zh: 那你就不用操心更新了。[绝对不是后期添加的通知音效]
cues.en: well you won’t need to worry about updates. [definitely-not-added-in-post notification sound]

cues.zh: 哎呀，看来我的灯泡又该更新固件了，
cues.en: Ope, looks like there’s a firmware update for my light bulbs again,

cues.zh: 最好赶紧动手！
cues.en: better get on that!

cues.zh: ♫ 乘法般顺滑的爵士乐 ♫
cues.en: ♫ multiplicatively smooth jazz ♫

cues.zh: 大家好，我接下来会继续探索这台微波炉的一些功能（还有它的一些小毛病）
cues.en: Hey there, I’ll be exploring some more of this microwave's features (and also its quirks)

cues.zh: 更随意地放在第二个频道。
cues.en: more casually on the second channel.

cues.zh: 各个地方都会放链接，不过现在，先来点小音效。
cues.en: There’ll be links in all the places but for now, le bloops.

cues.zh: ……在智能手机时代，我们在设计师微波炉领域见过的最有意思的东西——
cues.en: ...in the age of the smartphone, about the most interesting thing we’ve seen come to the designer microwave oven space -

cues.zh: 东西。已经来了！
cues.en: things. Already!

cues.zh: 最有趣的一点是我们……东西！
cues.en: About the most interesting thing we’ve s… things!

cues.zh: 我又忘了那个 s……！
cues.en: I forgot the s… again!

cues.zh: 而且它们总是有效。她最喜欢的……不对不对，从没失败过。
cues.en: And they always worked. Her favorite… nah nuh, never failed.

cues.zh: 别改词！
cues.en: Don’t change the words!

cues.zh: 脚本是你写的，校对也是你做的，为什么读的时候还要改词？
cues.en: You wrote the script, you proofread it, why are you changing the words as you read it?

cues.zh: 你个笨蛋。
cues.en: You doofus.

cues.zh: 要做一些美味的蓝色果冻。
cues.en: Gonna make some delicious blue jigglies.

cues.zh: 非常 fred……fred？
cues.en: Very fred… fred?

cues.zh: Fred Kindley。
cues.en: Fred kindley.

cues.zh: “嗨，我是 Fred Kindley。”
cues.en: "Hi, I’m Fred Kindley."

cues.zh: 说正经的，这是 p……说正经的，这……说正经的，这……
cues.en: In seriousness though, this is p… in seriousness though this... in seriousness though thi....

cues.zh: 说正经的。
cues.en: In seriousness.

cues.zh: 我为什么要写那个？
cues.en: Why did I write that?

cues.zh: 就看看家装店里卖的微波炉。
cues.en: Just look at microwaves for sale in a home improvement store.

cues.zh: 没有一台像 advsvsvvsvsvsvsvs 那样。
cues.en: None of them are as advsvsvvsvsvsvsvs.

cues.zh: [清嗓子] 好吧，这句要读一辈子了。
cues.en: [clears throat] well this line’s taking forever.

cues.zh: 别去谷歌搜那个。
cues.en: Don’t google that.

cues.zh: 它甚至还有。
cues.en: It evens got.

cues.zh: 哦糟了。
cues.en: Oh shoot.

cues.zh: 它甚至还有……
cues.en: It’s even got…

cues.zh: 它甚至还有普罗旺斯炖菜！
cues.en: it evens gots ratatouille!

cues.zh: 我对自己气炸了。
cues.en: I am beyond mad at myself.

cues.zh: 为什么？
cues.en: Why?

cues.zh: 因为这台微波炉真的是“超乎想象地自动”，而且这句不是我写在脚本里的
cues.en: Because this microwave oven truly is Automatic Beyond Belief and I DIDN'T WRITE THAT IN THE SCRIPT

cues.zh: 我怎么会这么粗心？
cues.en: how could I be so careless?

cues.zh: 我这是“零努力十一月”把自己给坑了。
cues.en: I No Effort Novemebered myself.
